headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, companies show mixed financial results with strong AI and digital rebuild activity.
summary: Media firms posted solid revenue growth, led by Disney, while some peers tighten spend. Gaming operators see divergent performance, with Caesars losing money and Bally's expanding revenue. Publishing shows a split, Pearson growing and Scholastic missing targets. Education players are mixed, highlighted by Pearson's gains and SLU's cost cuts.

industries.summary: Revenue growth is strong, especially at Disney. AI tools and platform consolidations are common. Some peers face tighter IT budgets.

leaders.why: Revenue of $25,947 m and 19.2% operating margin

laggards.why: Lowest operating margin at 5.2% and revenue decline YoY

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney launched AI search summaries and a trip‑planning tool; other firms cite AI pilots and partnerships.

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Hulu app retirement, FAST channel additions, and streaming membership launches reshape content delivery.

industries.it_note: Disney expands spend on AI and platform work, while WBD tightens budgets; account teams should balance growth opportunities with cost‑sensitivity.

industries.summary: Revenue is rising at Bally's and Caesars, but profitability varies. Cost‑cutting and debt reduction dominate many agendas.

leaders.why: Largest revenue at $2,940 m despite a net loss

laggards.why: Negative operating margin of -8.7% despite revenue growth

themes.title: Cost‑cutting & restructuring
themes.detail: Light & Wonder and Brightstar focus on debt reduction; Bally's refinances debt to improve liquidity.

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Caesars reports 5% digital revenue increase; Bally's integrates Intralot systems for new online offerings.

industries.it_note: IT spend is tightening at Caesars and Light & Wonder, but expanding at Bally's; prioritize efficiency projects while monitoring digital spend.

industries.summary: Pearson shows strong revenue and margin, while Scholastic misses targets. M&A activity and AI partnerships are notable.

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Pearson expands AI credentials; Wolters Kluwer partners with Viz.ai and acquires AgileMD.

themes.title: M&A activity
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer's AgileMD deal and Warner Bros./Paramount studio merger illustrate consolidation.

industries.it_note: Both Pearson and Wolters Kluwer are increasing technology spend on AI and platform integration; account teams should explore partnership opportunities.

industries.summary: Pearson drives growth, while SLU cuts staff and outsources services. New program pilots appear at NYU.

laggards.why: Full custodial staff layoffs and outsourcing indicate cost pressure

themes.title: Cost restructuring
themes.detail: SLU outsources custodial services; Pearson announces major business restructure.

themes.title: Program innovation
themes.detail: NYU pilots shuttle‑bus service and proposes three‑year bachelor degrees.

industries.it_note: IT spend is unclear overall; Pearson expands, while SLU likely tightens. Focus on supporting restructuring and new pilot initiatives.
